subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser login handoff surface be a first-party Control UI panel or browser-plugin tab, and what permissions should separate passive viewing from tab/write actions?
rationale: The feature crosses authenticated browser state, Control UI auth, plugin UI ownership, and agent resume policy; automation cannot safely choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: First-party read-only-first panel
options.body: Add a secured Control UI browser handoff panel that shows status/tabs/context by default and requires explicit operator steps for focus, navigation, clicks, credential entry, and submit actions.

options.title: Browser plugin tab after API hardening
options.body: Wait for a maintained plugin UI entry contract, then implement the browser surface as a browser-plugin-owned tab under explicit Gateway scopes and sandbox rules.

options.title: Defer to CLI/RPC only
options.body: Keep the existing browser CLI and browser.request primitives while deferring visible handoff until browser preview becomes a prioritized product area.

recommendation.title: First-party read-only-first panel
recommendation.body: Add a secured Control UI browser handoff panel that shows status/tabs/context by default and requires explicit operator steps for focus, navigation, clicks, credential entry, and submit actions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already identified this as the canonical handoff tracker and has the strongest combined browser runtime, docs, and product-routing signal in the reviewed evidence.
